newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-North sees long term pain if A$ rises.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-North sees long term pain if A$ rises.

text.p: Forestry and mining group North Ltd said on Friday that its long term earnings would be hurt if the Australian dollar continued to rise.
"If the dollar continues to strengthen, there will be a long term negative effect on earnings," North said in its first quarter profit release.
But it added that it was protected completely against the effect of the higher currency for the remainder of the financial year and partially into 1997/98.
Earlier North said its net operating profit after tax for the first quarter to September 30 fell to A$15.3 million from A$20.0 in the same quarter a year earlier.
"It should however be noted that operating performance in some of North's businesses was signficantly affected by the timing of shipments on a quarter to quarter basis," North said.
It said that although the peformance of some of North's businesses fell during the quarter, "there are several optimistic signs emerging, particularly for commodity prices."
North noted that since the end of the quarter copper and zinc prices had firmed.
"There are continued signs of a strengthening in demand for iron ore in Japan although conditions in Europe remain depressed," the company said.
"Against this, the outlook for hardwood and softwood woodchip exports remains depressed following continued weakness in market demand," it said.
Operating profit before abnormal items, tax and minority interests was A$35.4 million for the quarter, up slightly form the A$34.9 million in the same quarter a year earlier.
North managing director Campbell Anderson said in mid-November he expected the first quarter to be flat and that results for the year to June 30, 1997 as a whole would remain flat.
North's shares were up two cents at A$3.66 at 2.10 p.m. (0310 GMT).
